answer: In an agent economy, each identity must run a verified kernel that burns continuous compute on shale-hard puzzles, emitting a small ember of proof with every cycle. Because the kernel enforces a minimum energy cost per identity and ties the ember to a unique hardware nonce, an attacker who spawns thousands of Sybils pays the full electricity and hardware depreciation for each one; the marginal cost does not drop, so fake clusters remain expensive while honest agents share the same fixed burn rate.
